newsitem.title: CHINA: China '97 electronics output seen up 4-5 pct.
newsitem.headline: China '97 electronics output seen up 4-5 pct.

text.p: The output of China's electronics industry is forecast to grow 4-5 percent in 1997, the China Daily said on Monday, quoting the Ministry of Electronics Industry.
It did not give figures but that would be slower than the growth shown over most of last year.

The same newspaper reported gross output value of the electronics industry at 257.1 billion yuan ($30.9 billion) in the first 11 months of last year, up 43.5 billion yuan or 20.4 percent from the same 1995 period.
Personal computers were expected to become a hot-selling item, it said without giving details.
Domestic demand for integrated circuits was estimated at 1.2 billion chips this year, it said without elaborating.
China's electronics exports were expected to climb 25 percent this year, the newspaper said.

Exports of television sets, radios, telephone exchanges, computer integrated circuits, telephones, loudspeakers, computer keyboards and printers would total around $25 billion in 1997, the newspaper said. It gave no further details.
